items.title: Oscar Peterson interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: we were on the tour with him, © Fillius Jazz Archive -8- and he had the big band and I had the trio.

ctx.x: And that band was, Louie Bellson was telling me that that band was tailored for itself. It was individual. And he said when he got in the band, he looked in the drum book and he couldn’t find any parts in there. And he went to Duke and he said, “Duke, you know, how am I going to play these things.” And Duke said, “well with a man with your kind of musical intelligence, it should be no problem.” Duke was responsible for me doing some solo work. He said, I remember one night I’d come out, we were on the tour with…

and he had the big band and I had the trio. And we were getting ready to leave. And he was standing in the wings with Norman Granz and myself and he said “tell me,” he used to call me the Maharaja of the piano, you see, “tell me, Maharaja,” he said, “have you given any thought” — I think Norman had instigated him, he was trying to get me to play solo piano, and I kept saying na, na, na, I want to play trio piano.
